entries.summary: No verified material change versus the 21:14 EST assessment. Thursday cash closes remain Nasdaq -0.39%, SOX -0.54%, NVDA -4.34%, AMD +5.86%, AVGO +5.54%. November 13 October PPI remains pending at 08:30 EST. Fresh November 13 pre-release calendar reporting confirms the event, but not an actual PPI value or synchronized US overnight quotes. Curated Open Watch contains 159 events, last updated 2026-11-12T23:58:32+00:00. Bias remains Bearish — Elevated Downside Risk; Moderate-Low confidence, Very High event risk.
bullish: Nasdaq closed -0.39% after opening -1.47%, showing substantial absorption of the initial Nvidia shock.
AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54% at Thursday's close indicate selective chip rotation rather than uniform sector capitulation.
Foxconn and Siemens data-center demand signals remain supportive of longer-run AI infrastructure spending; no attributable index response is established.

Applied Materials fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS $4.16 versus $4.06 expected and revenue $10.41B versus $10.3B; next-quarter guidance above estimates. Cisco reported adjusted EPS $1.40 versus $1.33 expected, revenue $18.5B versus $18.1B and raised outlook; positive AI networking demand evidence, not proof of Friday market response.
bearish: Nvidia closed -4.34% following the confirmed CEO transition, and SOX finished -0.54%; leadership and semiconductor benchmark remain vulnerable.
Higher oil and long yields reported earlier remain valuation risks, but current synchronized oil/yield measurements are missing.
Reuters reports at least a 25bp December Fed hike fully priced, with a 15% chance of a 50bp move; hotter PPI could worsen duration-sensitive equity pressure.
Applied Materials was reportedly nearly flat after hours despite its beat after falling 3.6% in regular trade; a strong report alone has not confirmed sector-wide risk appetite.

editorial.marketOverview: Nasdaq -0.39%, SOX -0.54% and NVDA -4.34% at Thursday's close remain the latest verified US cash-session signals. AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54% show rotation within semiconductors rather than uniform capitulation. Cisco and Applied Materials earnings were constructive for AI infrastructure demand but their Friday cash-session impact is unobserved. No fresh synchronized overnight quote set establishes a different risk regime.
editorial.whatChanged: Relative to the 21:14 EST assessment, the November 13 economic-release calendar independently reconfirms US October PPI as a pending event. No actual release, timestamp-matched market repricing, or newly curated Open Watch catalyst is verified. Existing observations age further; this is a data-freshness update, not a directional change.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Bearish risk remains elevated due to NVDA leadership fragility, rate sensitivity and inflation-event risk. Thursday's partial Nasdaq recovery and strength in AMD and AVGO prevent high conviction in a broad sector breakdown. The market's actual response to PPI and AMAT/CSCO matters more than an expected impact inferred from earnings.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 13: verify 08:30 EST October PPI actual and consensus, matched Treasury yields, then QQQ/SOX breadth and reaction to AI infrastructure earnings. Monday November 16: test semiconductor follow-through versus renewed NVDA weakness. Tuesday November 17: seek multi-session confirmation or reversal. Scenarios are conditional, not price forecasts.
editorial.bullCase: A benign PPI surprise with easing matched yields, NVDA stabilization and sustained QQQ/SOX relative strength could validate a broader recovery. AMD and AVGO strength plus positive AI infrastructure earnings provide a foundation, but require market confirmation.
editorial.bearCase: A hotter-than-expected PPI, higher yields, renewed NVDA/SOX weakness, worsening breadth and rising VXN/VIX would support a deeper drawdown. Higher oil would compound the inflation channel only if fresh observations confirm it.
editorial.watchNext: Confirm official PPI release at 08:30 EST, then obtain timestamp-matched QQQ/Nasdaq, SOX, NVDA, AMD, AVGO, AMAT, CSCO, 10Y/2Y, VXN/VIX, breadth, Brent/WTI and FedWatch. Monitor curated Open Watch changes and distinguish expectations from realized price reaction.
